subject: alpha level does not work on R for Mac

messages.author: f8151fe12a4e4b33
messages.subject: alpha level does not work on R for Mac
parts:
Hello
I am trying to follow the examples in the ggplot2 book. So far I am
finding that everything works well except for the alpha scaling-- used
to compensate for overplotting of dense data points or lines.

The following lines for instance taken from chapter 9 almost
replicates the correct figure (Fig 9.7, Left) -- all colours are
correct but there is no alpha scaling sadly.

>pcp_cl=ggplot(molten, aes(variable,value, group=.row, colour=cluster))
> pcp_cl + geom_line(position = jit, alpha= 1/5)

Indeed all the examples involving alpha scaling do not work for me.
Has anyone else had this problem or perhaps has a solution- Mac or
otherwise?


Thanks
Stephen Henderson
UCL

messages.author: 6478aa6c7820c75e
messages.subject: Re: alpha level does not work on R for Mac
parts:
Alpha requires a display type which supports it, and most notably won't work in an X11() display.  Try Quartz, Cairo or PDF displays if you require Alpha transparency.

Jonah

messages.author: b26ea422f70d3a1f
messages.subject: Re: alpha level does not work on R for Mac
parts:
I just noticed this thread, and I don't think that it's been pointed
out so far, but it appears that you're using a 64-bit version
("x86_64") of R. Which raises two issues:

1. As far as I know, CRAN Mac binaries are 32-bit, which might mean
that you're using an R compiled from source by someone else. Which
might explain some differences. The example works on my 32-bit version
("i386") of R 2.9.2 from CRAN.

2. I wonder if ggplot or anything it depends on has a bug that causes
problems when you compile it 64-bit or link in 64-bit versions of
other libraries.
